title: What Spatial Operating Systems Is
definition: Spatial Operating Systems: oSes organizing work in 3D space.
description:
Spatial Operating Systems is oSes organizing work in 3D space. It sits squarely in Future Software Paradigms, the frontier where spatial shells science becomes OS logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are gesture vocab-scale. Societies that master OS hulls early will shape room mapping practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why spatial shells programs worldwide now treat Spatial Operating Systems as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Spatial Operating Systems needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Spatial Operating Systems
title: Real Research Today: Spatial Operating Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Spatial Operating Systems.
description:
The road to Spatial Operating Systems is already being paved. Projectional editing (JetBrains MPS) lets languages reshape the editor itself. Unikernel and library-OS research (MirageOS) rebuilds operating systems as composable libraries.

Formal methods adoption grows in aerospace (NASA), chips (Intel/ARM) and crypto protocols. Together these programs form the spatial shells foundation that Spatial Operating Systems will build on — the OS logistics results, the room mapping methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as OS logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Spatial Operating Systems
definition: Estimates Spatial Operating Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Spatial Operating Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a OS hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Spatial Operating Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Spatial Operating Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Spatial Operating Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 65152 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where spatial shells monitoring, OS logistics redundancy, or room mapping maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Spatial Operating Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Spatial Operating Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Spatial Operating Systems — oSes organizing work in 3D space.

Phase 1 — Prove (spatial shells): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (OS logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (room mapping): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (gesture vocab): OS hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and AR users-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
